title: Every Hour, They Walk Into 100 MPH Winds
asof: Figures from Mount Washington Observatory & FOX Weather · full video on the channel

shots.s: Every hour, someone walks out into this.
The top of Mount Washington, in New Hampshire.
The weather station here isn't automated. Ice and wind wreck the instruments.
So every hour, day and night, an observer goes outside.
One said the only time they don't go out is lightning.
They climb the tower, about a hundred feet up,
and knock the ice off with a rubber mallet or a crowbar.
In 1934, observers here measured a gust of two hundred thirty-one miles an hour.
Could you go out there every hour?
